title: Convert DR exercise evidence into maintained readiness
summary: An exercise creates value only when observations become accountable findings, corrective actions, maintained plans, and retests that improve recovery readiness.
outcome: Given DR exercise evidence, classify findings, assign corrective action, communicate status, update the plan, and define a retest that demonstrates closure.
managerMindset: Treat exercise findings as risk decisions with owners and evidence, not as a report that becomes obsolete when the meeting ends.

sections.title: Turn observations into defensible findings
sections.body: Capture the objective, planned condition, observed condition, evidence, timing, participants, deviation, consequence, and confidence. Separate a documentation issue from a capability failure and a process or ownership failure; each requires different remediation. Classify findings by impact and urgency, link them to the recovery assumption they challenge, and communicate test status to the right stakeholders, including regulators or customers when required. Do not claim a plan passed simply because the exercise completed on schedule.
keyPoints: Evidence should support both what happened and what the exercise could not test.
A finding needs a consequence or risk statement, not just a description of inconvenience.
Test status communications must distinguish exercise success, capability success, and unresolved risk.

sections.title: Maintain the plan and prove closure
sections.body: Assign each material finding an accountable owner, corrective action, due date, dependency, acceptance evidence, and risk disposition. Update contacts, diagrams, procedures, assumptions, supplier commitments, training, and recovery configuration under change control. A retest should target the failed condition, use a proportionate form, and define evidence that the action closed the gap rather than merely changing a document. Track overdue or accepted exceptions and schedule the next exercise when system, supplier, threat, or business conditions change.
keyPoints: Plan maintenance is a controlled change with version, approval, and communication evidence.
Closure means the intended capability or decision works, not that an action was marked complete.
Retest scope should be large enough to verify the fix and small enough to isolate what changed.

workedExamples.title: Unreachable recovery contact
workedExamples.situation: A tabletop shows that the alternate site contact is no longer employed. The owner updates a contact list but does not test the backup channel or the supplier's escalation path.
workedExamples.reasoning: Classify the issue as a people and communication capability gap, assign a primary and alternate owner, test the approved channels, update the plan version, and retest contact activation. Evidence must show that the team can reach the decision authority during an event, not only that a name was replaced.

distinctions.difference: An observation records what was seen; a finding interprets the gap, consequence, and required decision or action against the exercise objective.
Corrective action changes the capability or process that caused a gap; a plan update records the current executable method and assumptions.
Closure demonstrates that the intended fix works; risk acceptance documents an authorized decision to retain an unresolved gap with conditions.

misconceptions.misconception: Updating the DR document closes a failed exercise finding.
misconceptions.correction: A document update is only closure when the underlying capability, ownership, or decision has been made executable and retested.

misconceptions.misconception: Lessons learned are informal notes for the next exercise.
misconceptions.correction: Material lessons need owners, deadlines, evidence, change control, and risk disposition.

recallChecks.prompt: What should a defensible finding contain?
recallChecks.answer: Objective, expected and observed conditions, evidence, deviation, consequence or risk, confidence, owner, and required decision or action.
Evidence that the changed capability or process meets the stated acceptance criterion in a proportionate retest.

recallChecks.prompt: When should a plan be retested or refreshed?
recallChecks.answer: After material findings and when systems, suppliers, people, threats, regulations, or business priorities change.

scenarioSeeds.scenario: A full-interruption exercise was stopped safely, but the recovery team did not test customer communications or regulator notification.
scenarioSeeds.decision: Record the exercise as partially successful, assign communication and regulatory actions, update the scope and contact plan, and schedule a targeted retest.
scenarioSeeds.why: A safe stop is valuable evidence but does not prove the untested stakeholder path.

studyPlan.learn: Study exercise evidence, findings, corrective actions, lessons learned, plan maintenance, retest, and stakeholder or regulator communication.
studyPlan.connect: Connect D7.12 to D6 reporting and remediation, D7.11 DR process, D7.10 capabilities, D1 risk acceptance, and D7.13 continuity exercises.
studyPlan.apply: Convert one exercise observation into a finding, owner, acceptance criterion, corrective action, and retest plan.
studyPlan.revisit: Explain why an updated document can still leave the recovery capability unproven.

visualLearningContract.teachingQuestion: How does an exercise observation become a verified, owned, and retested recovery improvement?
visualLearningContract.misconception: Finishing on time, updating a plan, or logging an issue proves recovery readiness.
visualLearningContract.formRationale: Aligned columns make concept meanings, decision criteria and failure consequences explicit and comparable.
visualLearningContract.focalInsight: Observation, evidence, finding, owner/action, plan change, retest, and truthful test status.
visualLearningContract.intentionalOmissions: Do not prescribe a universal severity scale, retention duration, or external reporting rule.
visualLearningContract.retrievalPrompt: An observer says “the team seemed confused”; what evidence is needed before creating a DR finding, and what closes it?
visualLearningContract.textFallback:
test evidence: Time-stamped artifacts that substantiate what was attempted, observed, decided, and achieved in a test.. Decision: Collect evidence tied to the objective and protect its integrity before interpreting a pass/fail result.. Failure/example: A verbal claim that “failover worked” cannot establish recovery time, data state, or authorization.
exercise observation: A recorder’s factual note about behavior, timing, deviation, or condition during an exercise.. Decision: Record facts and context first; do not label it a failure until the expected condition and evidence are compared.. Failure/example: Treating an uncorroborated impression as a finding can send remediation at the wrong problem.
dr finding: A validated gap between an expected recovery condition and observed evidence, with stated impact and confidence.. Decision: Classify it by capability, documentation, process, or ownership and link it to the challenged recovery assumption.. Failure/example: A finding with no stated consequence cannot be prioritized or accepted as risk.
corrective action: A specific change assigned to an accountable owner to address a validated finding, with due date and acceptance evidence.. Decision: Assign action only after the finding is understood; record dependencies and an explicit risk disposition if it cannot be completed.. Failure/example: “Update DR plan” without owner or acceptance test creates an untrackable promise.
lessons learned: A reusable conclusion that explains why the observed result occurred and changes future recovery decisions or capability.. Decision: Derive lessons from supported findings across the exercise; avoid turning blame or a single anecdote into a general rule.. Failure/example: A blame-focused lesson discourages reporting and leaves the system condition unchanged.
plan maintenance: Controlled updating of contacts, assumptions, diagrams, procedures, and commitments as conditions change.. Decision: Update the plan through change control after a verified need; identify which plan element and dependency changed.. Failure/example: A stale contact list can make an otherwise sound recovery design unusable during activation.
retest: A proportionate repeat exercise that demonstrates the specific corrected condition now works.. Decision: Retest the failed path and predefined acceptance evidence, not merely a different easy scenario.. Failure/example: Closing a ticket after editing a document without exercising the changed handoff leaves the capability unverified.
test status: An accurate statement of what scope/objectives passed, failed, were untested, or remain at risk.. Decision: Communicate status with scope and limitations to the appropriate decision makers; never equate schedule completion with readiness.. Failure/example: A blanket “passed” report can cause leaders to accept recovery risk they were never shown.
regulator communication: A governed disclosure to a regulator about exercise status or material gaps when a legal, contractual, or supervisory obligation applies.. Decision: Use counsel/compliance-approved triggers, audience, timing, and facts; do not invent a reporting duty from the exercise alone.. Failure/example: An unapproved disclosure can be inaccurate or omit required facts; silence can breach an applicable duty.
